_comment: SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH — edit only this file. All components read from it.

vulnboxes.name: edge-proxy
vulnboxes.note: PLACEHOLDER host entry, generated from the organizer's credential sheet (SSH admin access only -- it does not list the actual challenge ports). Fill in services[] once you've SSH'd in and found what's actually listening (ss -tlnp / docker ps). capture_ssh_alias is an alias you create in ~/.ssh/config (key-based, NOT the root password from the credential sheet -- see docs/GOLIVE.md multi-host section).

vulnboxes.name: gitea
vulnboxes.note: PLACEHOLDER -- same as edge-proxy. Likely fronts a Gitea instance; fill in services[] once confirmed.

vulnboxes.name: jenkins
vulnboxes.note: PLACEHOLDER -- same as edge-proxy. Likely fronts a Jenkins instance; fill in services[] once confirmed.

vulnboxes.name: dns-ops
vulnboxes.note: PLACEHOLDER -- same as edge-proxy. Likely a DNS service -- if so its challenge port is probably udp/53, not tcp; ctf_proxy can't front UDP (see CONFIG.md's content-based iptables fallback).

monitor_host.bind_ip_note: Address the Dashboard (8080) and Tulip web UI (3000) listen on. 127.0.0.1 = only this machine (safe default). Set to a LAN IP to let teammates on a trusted network open them. Redis (6380), the detection admin/test API (9998), and Tulip's Postgres (5433) are ALWAYS loopback-only regardless of this value -- all three are unauthenticated, so they never follow bind_ip. The honeytoken port always listens on all interfaces by design.
monitor_host.note: CHANGE_ME: this machine's address on the SoftEther VPN once connected (verify with `ip -4 addr show` on the VPN's virtual NIC -- NOT the home-LAN/wifi address). Needed for honeytoken/OS-watchdog push (pull fallback works regardless, see docs/RUNBOOK.md's one-way-routing section).

flag.note: CSCV2026 rCTF scoreboard -- flag format and submit endpoint not in the credential sheet (it only has the team token, used to log into rCTF's own web UI, not a flag-submit API like ForcAD's). Check the rCTF scoreboard UI itself once reachable; rCTF typically wants you to submit flags through its own web page rather than a PUT-with-header API -- confirm before assuming the old ForcAD-style submit_url flow applies here at all.

gameserver_hint.note: rCTF scoreboard (not ForcAD -- different platform, different submit flow, see flag.note above). Team token for logging into it is in the organizer's credential sheet, kept OUT of this file.

honeytoken.note: a fake flag placed in a trap file on a vulnbox; if seen outbound it means compromise. Format should match flag.regex once that's filled in -- update this value to match.

tulip.note: Tulip stores flows in TimescaleDB/Postgres, not Mongo

mock_vulnbox.note: false = real vulnboxes (see vulnboxes[] above). bringup.sh skips the toy app + ctf_proxy when false.

ctf_proxy.note: Global ctf_proxy settings, shared across every vulnbox entry's own independent ctf_proxy deployment -- keyword MUST stay the single source other tools read from, do not hardcode elsewhere. Per-host insertion details (which compose file/service/network on THAT host) now live on each vulnboxes[] entry's own ctf_proxy_insertion, not here.

ml_classifier.note: Do NOT enable during contest unless BTC has confirmed in writing; encoder/clustering classifier only, never generative. This flag has NO EFFECT when MODE=contest regardless of its value — bringup.sh never passes docker-compose.prep.yml (where ml-fingerprint lives) in contest mode, full stop. Only meaningful when MODE=prep.

retention.note: host_agent deletes captured pcaps in traffic/ (oldest first) only when needed: traffic/ grows past pcap_max_gb, or the disk has less than min_free_gb free. pcap_keep_minutes > 0 additionally deletes anything older than that (0 = off). Files younger than 10 min are never touched. Flows already imported stay in Tulip. On each vulnbox, pcaps are removed as soon as they are pulled. If min_free_gb is still violated after pcap cleanup, host_agent next prunes Docker's own dangling images/build-cache (always safe -- see contest-runtime/hostagent/retention.py). tulip_flow_retention_hours is a LAST-RESORT, opt-in-only escalation beyond that: 0 (default) = never touch Tulip's own flow data; set to e.g. 8 to let host_agent drop TimescaleDB chunks older than that many hours if disk is still critically low after everything else -- this deletes real captured contest flows, so leave it 0 unless you understand that tradeoff.
